settle: The verdict follows the registered conditions, but the placebo was not null. The vegetation share 200 to 300 m away predicts sensor temperature as strongly as the share within 50 m, so the data show that greener parts of a neighbourhood are cooler in the afternoon and do not show that the vegetation within 50 m is the cause. Three things would separate these: canopy and impervious cover from the city's 2017 LiDAR land cover (canopy apart from grass, close in time to the sensors), with building height and street width held fixed; a distance-decay analysis of the NDVI already cached, by rings from 0 to 500 m; and a change design, in which sensors (or the 2022 and later heat-mapping traverses) are compared before and after planting or removal recorded in Forestry Tree Points (hn5i-inap).

notes:
423 sensors with imagery (all had 100% of the 50 m disc), 420 sensors and 86451 sensor-days in 5043 NTA-by-day cells with at least two sensors; 354 sensors lie under 19 July 2022 tiles and 69 under 15 September tiles; no disc mixes dates. The 50 m vegetation share has mean 22.5%, SD 14.9 points (12.7 within NTA and flight date), and 12% of sensors are at 40% or more. Street-tree mounts average 24.7% and light-pole mounts 16.7%. Sensitivity: 100 m share -0.28 (-0.35 to -0.22); mean NDVI within 50 m -0.42 (-0.52 to -0.32) C per 0.1; 15 September tiles only -0.15 (-0.25 to -0.04); street-tree mounts -0.21 (-0.25 to -0.17); light-pole mounts -0.21 (-0.36 to -0.06); days with Central Park maximum at or above 30 C -0.24 (-0.29 to -0.18); with the street-tree count in the model -0.20 (-0.25 to -0.15), and the count itself -0.03 (-0.13 to 0.07) C per 10 trees. Placebo: ring share alone -0.35 (-0.45 to -0.25); jointly, ring -0.24 (-0.34 to -0.15) and 50 m share -0.17 (-0.22 to -0.13). Descriptive bins against under 10%: 10-20% -0.08 (-0.26 to 0.10), 20-30% -0.22 (-0.43 to -0.00), 30-40% -0.36 (-0.60 to -0.12), 40% and over -0.82 (-1.10 to -0.54) C. Unregistered check of georeferencing: within 5 m of the sensor the vegetation share is 0.59 at street-tree mounts and 0.11 at light-pole mounts. Limits stated in the registration apply: imagery three to four years after the temperatures, uncalibrated NDVI, grass counted with canopy, sensors sited in 23 high-vulnerability NTAs. The afternoon temperatures had been used by the earlier claim before this registration; the vegetation values had not been seen.

After the referee (13 Nov 2026): what is confirmed is the association and not the causal edge. The vegetation share 200 to 300 m away stays as large as the local share in every model, as the settle field already says. The referee reproduced the estimate and it survives clustering by NTA (-0.261 to -0.141), other NDVI thresholds and leaving out one NTA. A model with all rings together gives -0.165 (-0.214 to -0.115) for 0 to 25 m, nothing from 25 to 200 m and -0.212 (-0.332 to -0.093) for 200 to 300 m; the ring widths were chosen after the data. An alternative not addressed is shade on the sensor housing as distinct from cooler air: all of the local association lies within 25 m, which fits shading of the instrument at least as well as cooling. The slope differs by year (-0.14 in 2018, -0.24 in 2019) with largely different sensors. The published temperature file is a balanced panel (every sensor-day has 7 of 7 afternoon hours), so it was gap-filled or cleaned before publication and the registered 5-of-7 filter removed nothing. On like-for-like radius the city slope is larger than Ziter's. The graph row for PMID 35060045 stores r = -1.0, which is not a published number; it was used for direction only.
verdict_note: The association is confirmed. Vegetation 200 to 300 m away predicts temperature as strongly as vegetation within 50 m, so the local causal reading is not supported.
